exposure: Antiretroviral therapy and prophylaxis during the antepartum, intrapartum and postpartum periods
outcome: Effectiveness of interventions to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HIV
cohort: 232 HIV-exposed infants born to HIV-infected mothers in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil
finding: The rate of vertical HIV transmission was 8.2%, and the combination of intrapartum and postpartum antiretroviral prophylaxis was associated with a decreased odds of transmission.
mod_finding: The study found that cesarean delivery, along with other interventions, significantly reduces vertical transmission of HIV.
